title: Nibbles trade places
prompt:
A nibble is four bits: half a byte, and exactly one hex digit. Swapping the two nibbles of `0xa7` gives `0x7a`.

The starter reads a value typed in hex into `value_r`. Keep only its low byte in `byte_r`, then build `swap_r` from `byte_r` with the two nibbles traded. `lsr` by 4 brings the high nibble down, `lsl` by 4 moves the low nibble up, and `orr` joins the halves. After the left shift the old high nibble sits above bit 7, so mask it away with `and` to keep the answer inside one byte.

With the sample input `a7` the program prints `0xa7 -> 0x7a`.

## what is checked

- `0xa7 -> 0x7a` for the sample input
- the program exits cleanly
- the nibbles move with `lsl` and `lsr`
- the right answer for other values, including 0, `ff`, and values wider than one byte
starter:
// trade the two nibbles (4-bit halves) of a byte
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(value_r, w19)
define(byte_r, w20)
define(swap_r, w21)

.data
fmt_hex:    .string "%x"
fmt_out:    .string "0x%02x -> 0x%02x\n"

.bss
.balign 4
value_m:    .skip 4

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_hex                // read a value typed in hex
        ldr     x1, =value_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =value_m
        ldr     value_r, [x9]

        mov     byte_r, 0                   // replace these placeholders
        mov     swap_r, 0

        // TODO: put the low byte of value_r in byte_r, then build swap_r
        // from byte_r with its high and low nibbles traded.

        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        mov     w1, byte_r
        mov     w2, swap_r
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
